query: how is it different from a shark
answer:
The main difference is that a dolphin is a mammal and a shark is a fish. They look alike because they evolved similar streamlined bodies for the same job, but they aren't closely related [1][2]. Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole on top of the head, so they have to come up to the surface. Sharks get oxygen from the water through gills and spend their whole lives underwater [1][3]. Dolphins are also warm-blooded and nurse their young with milk. Most sharks are cold-blooded, and their skin is covered in tiny tooth-like scales [3]. On the inside, a shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, while a dolphin has bones [2]. An easy way to tell them apart in the water is the tail: a dolphin's tail flukes are horizontal and move up and down, while a shark's tail fin is vertical and sweeps side to side [1].

One caveat: many sharks also give birth to live young, so live birth on its own isn't a reliable way to tell them apart. Nursing with milk and breathing air are the real mammal traits [2].
